questions.question: How is the Modulation Ratio-of-Ratios (R) mathematically defined in pulse oximetry?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The ratio normalizes AC by DC.
explanations.b: Correct. R is the normalized optical modulation of Red divided by Infrared.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Subtraction does not normalize pathlength or emitter intensity differences.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Wavelength ratio does not measure physiological absorption.

questions.question: Why do commercial pulse oximeters use empirical calibration curves rather than theoretical Beer-Lambert formulas alone?

answers.a: Because LEDs cannot emit pure single-frequency wavelengths
answers.b: Because biological tissue induces severe multiple optical scattering not modeled by simple Beer-Lambert absorption
answers.c: Because microcontrollers lack computational power to divide numbers
answers.d: Because arterial blood does not contain hemoglobin

explanations.a: Incorrect. LED spectral width is a minor secondary factor.
explanations.b: Correct. Rayleigh and Mie optical scattering through vascular tissue cause significant deviations requiring empirical calibration.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Embedded microcontrollers easily perform floating-point divisions.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Blood contains high concentrations of hemoglobin.

questions.question: If an op-amp in the Transimpedance Amplifier stage saturates at +3.3V power rails, what happens to the estimated SpO₂?

answers.a: SpO₂ remains 100% accurate because op-amps are ideal
answers.b: Signal clipping destroys the true AC peak-to-peak amplitude, causing severe estimation errors or invalid readings

explanations.a: Incorrect. Real op-amps have physical power rails that clip signals.
explanations.b: Correct. Rail clipping flattens peak amplitudes, invalidating the AC/DC ratio R and corrupting the SpO₂ calculation.
explanations.d: Incorrect. LED drive circuitry is independent of amplifier saturation.
